_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::contact#7. The rule holds: on a two-block mortar penalty deck, a gap of 0.1 and an exactly-touching start both converge through all ten steps, while an initial overlap of one tenth of an element aborts with 'The nonlinear solver did not converge!' from solver_nonlin_nox/4C_solver_nonlin_nox_problem.cpp before finalising a single step, with a full four-node active set already present at step 0. The residual half of the Signal is confirmed as an ordering rather than a number: the overlapping deck's NOX force norm at Nonlinear Solver Step 0 is more than an order of magnitude above the touching one, because the penalty is already pushing on a closed gap. The diagnostic half is fabricated: no MortarInterface prints 'initial penetration X.X > tolerance', CLAIMED_TOLERANCE_TEXT=0, and INITIAL_PENETRATION_IS_NAMED=no — the log mentions neither penetration nor overlap nor the interface, so nothing in it distinguishes this failure from any other non-convergence. That is what makes it worth a pitfall entry: the cause has to be found by inspecting the geometry, never by reading the error. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf).
expect_in_output: The nonlinear solver did not converge!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: start the upper block exactly touching instead of overlapping. That arm then converges through all ten steps and exits 0, so the non-convergence abort and the raised step-0 residual both disappear and the fixture must go red.
